hints.content: In order to evaluate $\dfrac{d}{dx}[f(x)\cdot g(x)]$ at $x=3$, we should first find an expression for $\dfrac{d}{dx}[f(x)\cdot g(x)]$ (for any input $x$) in terms of $f$, $g$, and their derivatives.

The derivative is given by **the product rule**:

$\begin{align}
\dfrac{d}{dx}[u(x)v(x)]&=\dfrac{d}{dx}[u(x)]v(x)+u(x)\dfrac{d}{dx}[v(x)]
\\\\
&=u'(x)v(x)+u(x)v'(x)
\end{align}$

So $\dfrac{d}{dx}[f(x)\cdot g(x)]=f'(x)g(x)+f(x)g'(x)$.

We can now plug $x=3$ into this expression:

$f'(3)g(3)+f(3)g'(3)$

We are given that $f(3)=-1$ and $f'(3)=0$.

Since $g(x)=x^3$, we know that $g(3)=27$ and $g'(3)=27$. [[☃ explanation 1]]

Let's plug in those values!

$(0)(27)+(-1)(27)=-27$

options.explanation:
### Finding $g(3)$

$\begin{align}
g(\blueD{3})&=(\blueD 3)^3
\\\\
&=27
\end{align}$

### Finding $g'(x)$

$\begin{align}
g'(x)&=\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^3\right)
\\\\
&=3x^{2}
\end{align}$

### Finding $g'(3)$

$\begin{align}
g'(\blueD{3})&=3(\blueD3)^2
\\\\
&=3\cdot 9
\\\\
&=27
\end{align}$
